findings.english_quote: In this moral context, 'endurance' suits the lack of staying power under trial.
findings.issue: The lexical record identifies the chosen rendering as 'endurance' and attributes deficient staying power to the sufferers, whereas the main text correctly describes their having no respite. The metadata thus records a different interpretation and adds a psychological claim not established by this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Update the chosen gloss to 'respite' and explain the absence of relief from torment. Preserve 'endurance' only as an explicitly distinguished alternative if retained.

findings.issue: The rendering incorporates bracketed οὕτως without disclosing that the selected working source marks it editorially. Readers cannot distinguish this marked material from unbracketed text.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the working rendering if desired, but add a note explaining that 'so' represents bracketed οὕτως in the supplied source and that its bracketed status is editorial, not fresh manuscript verification.

findings.english_quote: some with every kind of disorder
findings.issue: The translation incorporates bracketed πάσῃ as 'every kind of' without disclosing its marked editorial status.
findings.suggested_revision: Disclose that 'every kind of' represents bracketed πάσῃ in the selected working source. Do not silently remove it merely because it is bracketed.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τότε δοξάζουσι τὸν Κύριον ὅτι ἐμοὶ παρεδόθησαν
findings.english_quote: because they were handed over to me[i][h][g][f][e][d][c]
findings.issue: Seven notes are attached to the handover clause although they concern other clauses. In particular, 'Or' notes about seeing, taking charge, and suffering are presented at a location where they are not alternatives to the attached wording. Notes a and b likewise sit on 'Therefore' and 'righteous angels' rather than their stated subjects.
findings.suggested_revision: Attach each note to its actual subject: the speaking shepherd, angel of punishment, present-life torments, projects, heart idiom, faith in the Lord, initial seeing, taking charge, and other sufferings. Identify historical renderings as such rather than implying that they are alternatives to the handover clause.

findings.source_quote: ἐκ δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν δικαίων ἐστί, κείμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς τιμωρίας
findings.english_quote: He is one of the righteous angels appointed to carry out punishment.
findings.issue: The English attaches appointment to the plural group 'righteous angels.' The Greek singular κείμενος describes this particular angel, separately from his membership among the righteous angels.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'He is one of the righteous angels. He is appointed to oversee punishment.' Review this replacement before adoption.

findings.source_quote: οἱ δὲ ὑβριζόμενοι ὑπὸ ἀναξίων καὶ ἑτέραις πολλαῖς πράξεσι πάσχοντες
findings.english_quote: Some are insulted by unworthy people, and some suffer in many other ways.
findings.issue: The second 'some' introduces a separate group. In the selected source, being insulted and suffering in many other undertakings describe the same group. 'Ways' also removes the connection with undertakings that continues into the following discussion.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'Some are insulted by unworthy people and suffer in many other undertakings.' Review the wording for accessible English without separating the group.

findings.source_quote: ἐὰν δὲ μετανοήσωσι, τότε ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἔπραξαν πονηρά
findings.english_quote: When they repent[a], their evil deeds come back to mind.
findings.issue: 'When' replaces the explicit conditional 'if' with a temporal formulation that presents repentance as expected to occur. The standard edition preserves the condition, but the simplified edition does not independently preserve it.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'But if they repent, then the evil deeds they did come to mind.' Retain contextual 'repent' without adding a requirement of completed reform.

findings.source_quote: τότε ἐμοὶ παραδίδονται εἰς ἀγαθὴν παιδείαν
findings.english_quote: they are handed over to me so that I may correct and train them
findings.issue: The paraphrase conveys corrective training but omits the explicit positive qualification ἀγαθήν, 'good' or 'beneficial.' That qualification distinguishes this discipline within the punishment narrative.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: 'they are handed over to me for good correction and training.' Review the replacement for fidelity and readability.

findings.source_quote: Βλέπων οὖν αὐτὰ οὕτω μαστιγούμενα καὶ ταλαιπωρούμενα
findings.english_quote: When I saw them being whipped and made to suffer like this
findings.issue: The inferential connection οὖν, 'therefore/so,' is omitted. Similar explanatory connections are lost when παραλαμβάνει οὖν becomes 'He takes charge' and πολλοὶ γὰρ becomes 'Many.' These omissions remove explicit links in the source's reasoning rather than merely simplifying vocabulary.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore accessible connecting words, such as initial 'So,' 'So he takes charge,' and 'For many' or 'This is because many,' with each replacement reviewed in context.

findings.english_quote: In this moral context, 'endurance' suits the lack of staying power under trial.
findings.issue: The copied lexical record claims deficient endurance, whereas this edition renders absence of relief. It adds an unsupported claim about the sufferers' staying power and does not accurately document the simplified wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Record 'relief' as this edition's chosen rendering and explain the absence of respite. Explicitly distinguish any retained alternative interpretation.

findings.issue: The simplified edition silently omits bracketed οὕτως, although it belongs to the selected working text and is represented by 'so' in the standard edition. Its marked status does not by itself authorize silent deletion.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider restoring 'so pitiless' and disclose that 'so' represents editorially bracketed material in the selected source.

findings.english_quote: Some suffer from every kind of trouble.
findings.issue: The edition retains bracketed πάσῃ as 'every kind of' without identifying its editorial status in the working source.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-status note identifying the bracketed word. Retention of the selected working reading does not require claiming manuscript verification.

findings.issue: Marker a points to a note about the speaking shepherd, not repentance. The repentance note j and the other supplied notes have no matching markers in this edition. Consequently, the documented alternative for 'faith in the Lord' is not linked to its actual text.
findings.suggested_revision: Rebuild the simplified edition's note anchors independently. Link repentance to its contextual note, the shepherd identification to the shepherd, and the faith alternative to 'faith in the Lord'; remove or accurately locate historical-rendering notes.

findings.english_quote: Maintains strong punitive imagery of being beaten with lashes; fits the scene of harsh correction.
findings.issue: The lexical entry still labels 'scourged' as the chosen rendering, although this edition uses 'whipped.' Other copied entries likewise record standard-edition wording rather than this edition's choices, and no simplification decisions document these differences. The audit metadata therefore does not accurately identify the supplied simplified translation.
findings.suggested_revision: Update the edition-specific chosen glosses and document contextual simplifications, including 'whipped,' 'made to suffer,' 'relief,' and 'he judges rightly.' Retain prior standard choices only as clearly labeled history or comparison.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard text covers the selected source, but its metadata, note placement, and disclosure of bracketed material need correction. Independent review of the simplified text also identifies a changed condition, shifted appointment scope, separated participant group, and omitted qualifications and connections. Reader-facing service language and contextual repentance are compatible with current policy. This review concerns the supplied working source and records only; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. All suggested replacements require fresh review.
